name: status-model
title: The deliverable status: one machine-derived stage for the whole pack

research.description: Synthesis and devil's advocate over both briefs

msft.description: Reviewer brief: Microsoft, Extending GitHub Spec Kit

fowler.description: Reviewer brief: martinfowler.com, Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl

shape.description: The codified spec-section shape with sources and rules

spec.why: The owner reads the generated pack JSON and cannot see where the overall deliverable stands: node-level statuses are everywhere, but the pack-level status is a near-mute active-or-complete record-lifecycle flag. The concern is the JSON, not the wiki. Two axes were collapsed: record lifecycle (mutable or frozen) and delivery progress (where the work is).

stories.as: the owner reading a generated pack file
stories.want: one field at the top that says where the overall deliverable stands
stories.so: I know what is going on without adding up task statuses

stories.as: a future loop querying many packs
stories.want: a machine-verified deliverable stage on every pack
stories.so: I can list deliverables by stage and trust what I read

requirements.text: The pack MUST carry one machine-derived deliverable stage (drafted, planning, in_progress, blocked, awaiting_owner, in_review, delivered, superseded), computed as a total deterministic function of task states, decision states, question states, and review verdicts; written by the machine at every save; re-derived at load, and a mismatch between stored and derived stage MUST refuse the load naming both values.

scenarios.when: the machine saves or loads it
scenarios.then: the stage field equals the derivation, and a hand-edited stage is refused

requirements.text: loom status and loom next MUST report the deliverable stage as the headline line, with task counts (done, doing, todo, blocked) beside it.

An exhaustive guard test MUST drive every derivation branch and assert set equality between exercised stages and the documented vocabulary; the schema enum, the code constant, and the derivation must agree.

The superseded stage requires the supersedes link (Q-1). Until the owner decides, the stage exists in the vocabulary and the derivation omits it; the decision MUST be recorded before any implementation task for it runs.

The machine MUST report story drift in the coverage tier: requirements that serve no user story, and stories that no requirement serves. Reported, never blocking. Served means an explicit link (requirement gains an optional serves list of story ids), not a guess.

Stories MUST support owner-authored acceptance criteria (scenarios, same given/when/then shape and AC- id pattern as requirement scenarios, additive and optional). The machine MUST verify story ACs like all ACs: tasks accept them, A2 resolves them, coverage maps them; a story whose ACs are all met by done tasks is done.

scenarios.given: a story with acceptance criteria and a task that accepts one of them
scenarios.when: that task is done with evidence
scenarios.then: coverage reports the story AC as met; a story with all ACs met reports done

constraints.text: No engine behavior changes: this wave is the model, the page, the bridge, and the guards. The frozen status-vocabulary pack is reference only.
No accepted decisions at authoring: every decision ships proposed; the owner accepts or rejects after reading the research.

clarifications.question: Should packs carry a supersedes link to the pack they replace, making the spec-anchored chain of custody explicit and queryable?
Should user-facing output adopt the field's words (spec, plan, tasks) alongside ours (pack, pack sections), or keep this system's vocabulary alone?
Should stories carry a machine-derived satisfaction status (every served FR's acceptance criteria met by done tasks), reported in status and check output — with ACs staying on requirements?
clarifications.answer: Stories get owner-authored acceptance criteria directly (D-8). Derivation through FRs rejected (D-7).

out_of_scope: any change to loom commands, schemas, or state machines
semantic search over complete packs (a future consumer)
rebuilding the wiki status vocabulary page: the owner states the wiki is fine (2026-10-09); D-1 and D-2 are rejected for this reason
the bridge table to field vocabulary (may return if the owner asks)

plan.approach: One derived field, verified like a checksum: derive, write on save, refuse on load mismatch. Headline reporting. Exhaustive branch guard. Supersedes stays gated on the owner.

stack.guards: pytest reading the schema and the page

designs.title: The deliverable stage derivation
designs.detail: A pure function over the pack: delivered (pack complete) > superseded (a supersedes link names this pack; gated on Q-1) > blocked (any task blocked, none doing) > awaiting_owner (all tasks done, decisions pending or questions open) > in_review (all tasks done, owner work clean, no PACK PASS) > in_progress (any task doing) > planning (open questions, no task done or doing) > drafted (tasks exist, none started, no open questions). First match wins; the function is total. The field name is deliverable. The record lifecycle keeps the existing status field: two axes, two fields, both machine-owned.

designs.title: Checksum discipline
designs.detail: load_specpack re-derives the stage and compares with the stored value. A mismatch raises with both values: a hand-edited stage is corruption, and the machine fails closed. Saves always write the derivation, so the field can never lag the content it summarizes.

designs.title: Headline reporting
designs.detail: loom status first line: the deliverable stage plus counts, for example 'deliverable: in_progress (3 done, 1 doing, 2 todo, 0 blocked)'. loom next prints the same line before any task output. The wiki page gains one row for the new family only if the owner asks for page work later.

designs.title: Story coverage: the served link and the drift report
designs.detail: Requirement gains an optional serves list (US id pattern). The coverage section gains story_drift: requirements with empty or missing serves, and stories named by no requirement. Reported, never blocking, consistent with the coverage-tier rule. Found by: the owner, 2026-10-09, after a re-scope left a stale story in a green-checked pack.

designs.title: Story acceptance criteria
designs.detail: Schema: story gains optional scenarios ($ref scenario, same def). alignment: A1 counts story ACs; A2 resolves accepts against the union of story and requirement scenarios; A5 coverage gains a US section mapping each story AC to the tasks that accept it. slices: story ACs ride along when the story is in the closure. Authoring rule: story ACs are few and intent-level; requirement scenarios verify the chosen solution.

designs.title: The spec anatomy in schema and checks
designs.detail: Additive schema: story gains title, priority, independent_test, acceptance (scenario shape, AC- ids); spec gains edge_cases, success_criteria (SC- id pattern), assumptions. Requirement gains serves (US ids) and scenarios becomes legacy-optional. Checks: A1 counts story ACs; A2 resolves task.accepts against story ACs and legacy FR scenarios; A4 alignment gains the story route (task accepts AC of US that FR serves); coverage maps story ACs and story done (all ACs met by done tasks).

decisions.decision: Rebuild the vocabulary page as three tables.
decisions.rejected_because: Owner, 2026-10-09: the wiki is fine; the concern is the pack JSON.

decisions.decision: The page carries a bridge from the field vocabulary.
decisions.because: Readers arrive with Spec Kit priors.
decisions.rejected_because: Owner, 2026-10-09: same directive; the wiki is not the concern.

decisions.decision: Machine-owned states stay, with field evidence as justification.
decisions.because: Fowler documents AI-interpreted checklist failure; transitions move only through loom commands.

decisions.decision: Packs gain a supersedes link; the superseded stage rides it.
decisions.because: Complete packs are frozen reference; today a new pack points at nothing, so lineage dies.

decisions.decision: The deliverable stage is machine-derived and checksum-verified, never owner-set.
decisions.because: An owner-set stage duplicates derived truth and drifts; the two axes (record lifecycle, delivery progress) get two fields: status stays lifecycle, deliverable carries progress.

decisions.decision: Stage vocabulary: drafted, planning, in_progress, blocked, awaiting_owner, in_review, delivered, superseded.
decisions.because: One word one meaning; each stage is separable by action: blocked needs a re-plan or unblock, awaiting_owner needs verdicts, in_review needs the closing PASS.

decisions.decision: Stories gain a derived satisfaction status, reported not authored; acceptance criteria stay on requirements (single-parent chain: task accepts AC, AC belongs to one FR, FR serves a US).
decisions.because: A story is satisfied when every FR it serves has its ACs met by done tasks — computable, so it must not be hand-set (the Fowler evidence against interpreted statuses). Putting ACs on stories would blur what an AC verifies. The third instance of the rollup disease (deliverable stage, orphaned stories, story satisfaction) closes the class.
decisions.rejected_because: Wrong altitude: deriving story-done from served FRs reads the solution, not the intent. A story can be done with a requirement descoped; derivation cannot express that. Atlassian's 3 C's put the Confirmation on the story (owner direction, 2026-10-09, with source).

decisions.decision: Stories gain acceptance criteria (given/when/then scenarios, AC- ids, same shape as requirement scenarios). Story done is its ACs met by done tasks: direct, owner-authored, machine-verified. Requirement scenarios stay for capability verification. Tasks accept ACs wherever they live; each AC keeps exactly one parent.
decisions.because: Atlassian 3 C's: Confirmation (the AC) defines when the story is complete; the story and its AC are one unit. ACs are intent-altitude, requirement scenarios are solution-altitude. Owner direction with source, 2026-10-09.

decisions.decision: The spec section anatomy is: why, stories (title, as/want/so, priority, independent_test, acceptance as given/when/then), edge_cases, requirements (plain MUST, serves a story, no scenarios), success_criteria, constraints, questions, assumptions, out_of_scope. Story done = its ACs met by done tasks.
decisions.because: Three primary sources agree on the load-bearing parts: ACs live on the story (Atlassian 3 C's Confirmation; Spec Kit Acceptance Scenarios verbatim in templates/spec-template.md), priority and independent testability live on the story with the P1-alone-is-MVP rule (Spec Kit), requirements are plain MUST statements (Spec Kit FR-NNN, Kiro EARS), and success criteria and assumptions are spec-level sections we lack. Owner directive 2026-10-09: the spec, high level, codified.

tasks.title: Deliverable stage: derivation, field, load refusal
tasks.detail: Per DES-1 and DES-2: derive_deliverable(doc) pure function (stages per D-6, superseded omitted until Q-1); every machine save writes it; load_specpack re-derives and refuses on mismatch naming both values; schema gains the optional deliverable enum. Tests: one fixture per branch, mismatch refusal, save-then-load roundtrip.

verify.expect: exit 0 — every derivation branch, mismatch refusal, roundtrip; suite green

tasks.title: Headline reporting in status and next
tasks.detail: Per DES-3: loom status prints the deliverable stage plus counts as the first line; loom next prints the same line before task output; both --json paths include the field.

verify.cmd: cd engine/loom && uv run pytest -q tests/test_specpack_deliverable.py tests/test_specpack_cli.py
verify.expect: exit 0 — headline asserted in human and json paths

tasks.title: Exhaustive guard for the stage vocabulary
tasks.detail: Per FR-3: extend the status guard family: schema enum equals the code constant; an exhaustive fixture drives every branch of derive_deliverable and asserts set equality with the documented vocabulary (minus superseded until Q-1).

verify.cmd: cd engine/loom && uv run pytest -q tests/test_specpack_status.py
verify.expect: exit 0 — set equality, guard can fail

tasks.title: superseded stage and the supersedes link
tasks.detail: GATED on Q-1 (stays blocked until the owner decides D-4). If accepted: schema gains supersedes (pack name reference), derivation adds the superseded stage (checked when another pack names this one), status shows it. If rejected: record the rejection, keep the stage out of the vocabulary, cancel with the recorded reason.

verify.expect: exit 0 — per the owner verdict on Q-1

tasks.title: Story drift coverage: serves link and report
tasks.detail: Per DES-4: schema gains requirement.serves (optional, US id pattern); alignment coverage gains story_drift (requirements serving no story, stories served by no requirement); this pack's own FRs gain serves links as the first fixture; loom check prints the lines.

verify.expect: exit 0 — drift reported both directions, never a violation; suite green

tasks.title: Story acceptance criteria: schema, checks, coverage, slices
tasks.detail: Per DES-5 and FR-6: story.scenarios in the schema (optional, additive); A1/A2 treat story ACs as first-class; A5 coverage gains the US section; slice_for includes story ACs when the story is in the closure; this pack's own stories gain ACs as the first fixture (US-1 gets AC-4's parentage fixed accordingly). Tests: story AC accepted by a done task reports met; dangling story AC refused; story with all ACs met reports done.

verify.expect: exit 0 — story ACs first-class in A1/A2/A5 and slices; suite green

tasks.title: Spec anatomy: schema, checks, coverage, fixture
tasks.detail: Per DES-6 and D-9: schema additions (story: title, priority, independent_test, acceptance; spec: edge_cases, success_criteria, assumptions; requirement: serves; requirement.scenarios marked legacy in descriptions); A1/A2/A4 and coverage updated for story ACs and story-done; this pack's own spec section is recast into the new shape as the first live fixture (stories gain priority, independent_test, acceptance; FR scenarios move up or are dropped where redundant); spec-shape.json rules quoted into the primer.

verify.cmd: cd engine/loom && uv run pytest -q && cd .. && uv run loom check docs/specs/status-model
verify.expect: exit 0 — new anatomy validates, story ACs first-class, this pack green in the new shape
